::: {#fig-inverse-function}

```{r}
#| label: inverse-function-alt
#| include: false
fig_alt <- paste(
  "Two panels with labeled curves.",
  "In the first, the line y = 2x + 1 and its inverse,",
  "the line y = (x - 1) / 2,",
  "are mirror images across the dashed diagonal y = x,",
  "drawn at 45 degrees on equal axes.",
  "The point (3, 7) on the first line corresponds to the point (7, 3)",
  "on the second.",
  "In the second panel, the parabola y = x^2 is crossed twice",
  "by the dotted horizontal line y = 4, at x = -2 and x = 2."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: inverse-function-plot
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt
line_panel <- "f(x) = 2x + 1 and its inverse"
square_panel <- "h(x) = x^2 is not invertible"
panel_levels <- c(line_panel, square_panel)
as_panel <- function(panel) factor(panel, levels = panel_levels)

x_f <- seq(-2, 4, length.out = 101)
x_inverse <- seq(-3, 9, length.out = 101)
lines_data <- data.frame(
  panel = as_panel(line_panel),
  x = c(x_f, x_inverse, x_inverse),
  y = c(2 * x_f + 1, (x_inverse - 1) / 2, x_inverse),
  curve = rep(
    c("f", "inverse of f", "y = x"),
    times = c(length(x_f), length(x_inverse), length(x_inverse))
  )
)
x_square <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101)
square_data <- data.frame(
  panel = as_panel(square_panel),
  x = x_square,
  y = x_square^2,
  curve = "h"
)
marked <- data.frame(
  panel = as_panel(c(line_panel, line_panel, square_panel, square_panel)),
  x = c(3, 7, -2, 2),
  y = c(7, 3, 4, 4)
)
# equal ranges on both axes of the first panel keep y = x at 45 degrees
equal_range <- data.frame(
  panel = as_panel(line_panel),
  x = c(-3, 9),
  y = c(-3, 9)
)
labels_data <- data.frame(
  panel = as_panel(c(line_panel, line_panel, line_panel, square_panel)),
  x = c(1.2, 7, 7.5, 2.4),
  y = c(5.2, 0.6, 8.2, 4.6),
  label = c("f", "inverse of f", "y = x", "y = 4")
)
level_four <- data.frame(panel = as_panel(square_panel), y = 4)

inverse_function_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_blank(data = equal_range, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = rbind(lines_data, square_data),
    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = curve, linetype = curve)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    data = level_four,
    ggplot2::aes(yintercept = y),
    colour = "grey40",
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = marked, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y), size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = labels_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = label)
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "f" = "#0072B2",
      "inverse of f" = "#D55E00",
      "y = x" = "grey40",
      "h" = "#0072B2"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "f" = "solid",
      "inverse of f" = "solid",
      "y = x" = "dashed",
      "h" = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "y") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  htmltools::div(
    role = "img",
    `aria-label` = fig_alt,
    plotly::ggplotly(inverse_function_plot)
  )
} else {
  inverse_function_plot
}
```

Left: the [graph](#def-graph) of the [inverse function](#def-inverse-function) $f^{-1}$ is the graph of $f$ reflected across the line $y = x$, so $(3, 7)$ becomes $(7, 3)$.
Right: the horizontal line $y = 4$ meets the graph of $h(x) = x^2$ twice, at $x = -2$ and $x = 2$,
so $h$ has no inverse function.

:::
